headline_marked: Argentina vs Spain: [[BD celebrities share predictions]] for World Cup final
headline: Argentina vs Spain: BD celebrities share predictions for World Cup final
summary: From singer Alif Alauddin's viral 'committee' T-shirts to filmmaker Ashfaque Nipun's Barcelona connection, local stars weigh in on the epic showdown.
details: As the World Cup final between Argentina and Spain approaches, Bangladeshi celebrities are gearing up for the biggest night in football. With Brazil out of the tournament, many local stars have shifted their support to the defending champions, Argentina.

Singer Alif Alauddin, a passionate Argentina supporter, revealed she is the creator of the viral 'Amra Committeer Lok' (We are the committee people) T-shirts. The phrase, born from jokes about FIFA's perceived favoritism toward Argentina, became a popular trend among fans across the country.

Filmmaker Ashfaque Nipun describes the match as a clash between Barcelona's past and present. He notes that with Lionel Messi leading Argentina and several current Barcelona players in the Spain squad, the game feels like a battle of Barcelona legends versus current stars.

Singer Dola Rahman and her family are backing Argentina, expecting nationwide celebrations if they win. She plans to watch the match at home but is ready to head to the streets or TSC to dance and celebrate if Argentina lifts the trophy.

Actress Jannatul Sumaiya Heme, despite being a Brazil supporter, believes Argentina are the favorites to lift the trophy. She noted that Argentina's fighting spirit throughout the tournament has impressed her, despite her own team's exit.

Actor Irfan Sajjad is hoping for 'Messi magic' as Argentina chases a second consecutive title. He believes that achieving back-to-back World Cup triumphs would be a remarkable and magical achievement in football history.
caption:
Who will lift the World Cup? 🏆 BD celebrities are divided between Messi's magic and Spain's dominance!

As the World Cup final between Argentina and Spain approaches, Bangladeshi celebrities are gearing up for the biggest night in football. With Brazil out of the tournament, many local stars have shifted their support to the defending champions, Argentina.

Singer Alif Alauddin, a passionate Argentina supporter, revealed she is the creator of the viral 'Amra Committeer Lok' (We are the committee people) T-shirts. The phrase, born from jokes about FIFA's perceived favoritism toward Argentina, became a popular trend among fans across the country.

Filmmaker Ashfaque Nipun describes the match as a clash between Barcelona's past and present. He notes that with Lionel Messi leading Argentina and several current Barcelona players in the Spain squad, the game feels like a battle of Barcelona legends versus current stars.

Singer Dola Rahman and her family are backing Argentina, expecting nationwide celebrations if they win. She plans to watch the match at home but is ready to head to the streets or TSC to dance and celebrate if Argentina lifts the trophy.

Actress Jannatul Sumaiya Heme, despite being a Brazil supporter, believes Argentina are the favorites to lift the trophy. She noted that Argentina's fighting spirit throughout the tournament has impressed her, despite her own team's exit.

Actor Irfan Sajjad is hoping for 'Messi magic' as Argentina chases a second consecutive title. He believes that achieving back-to-back World Cup triumphs would be a remarkable and magical achievement in football history.

headline_marked: Iran's Supreme Leader: [[Trump's signature is worthless]]
headline: Iran's Supreme Leader: Trump's signature is worthless
summary: Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei says US breaches of a memorandum of understanding have stripped Donald Trump of all credibility.
details: Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei stated in a written statement on Saturday that repeated U.S. breaches of a memorandum of understanding had rendered President Donald Trump's signature "utterly worthless and devoid of credibility."
The statement comes as Washington and Tehran have exchanged strikes after a ceasefire agreement fell apart last week, raising fears of a return to all-out war.
Khamenei further warned that the United States should be aware that the Iranian nation and the "resistance front" possess "unforgettable lessons" for the US.
caption:
Is the US-Iran ceasefire dead? Iran's Supreme Leader calls Donald Trump's signature "utterly worthless."

Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei stated in a written statement on Saturday that repeated U.S. breaches of a memorandum of understanding had rendered President Donald Trump's signature "utterly worthless and devoid of credibility."

The statement comes as Washington and Tehran have exchanged strikes after a ceasefire agreement fell apart last week, raising fears of a return to all-out war.

Khamenei further warned that the United States should be aware that the Iranian nation and the "resistance front" possess "unforgettable lessons" for the US.
